name: Compound Basic Numerative (Decade + Single-digit)

dimensions.form: Decade + single-digit compound; hyphenated; lexically atomic
dimensions.meaning: Specifies cardinality from twenty-one to ninety-nine
dimensions.function: Same distribution as simple basic numeratives
dimensions.distribution: Determiner, factor, addition; resists internal coordination (*twenty and one)

1.definition: Specifies a cardinality formed by additive composition of tens and ones

constraints.description: Requires a decade base with a single-digit addition; excludes *twenty-ten.

projection.target: Forty-three expresses one lexicalized sum and supplies a base for forty-third. A coordinator inside forty and three produces a separate structure and is not the ordinary lexical compound.
projection.evidence: Reynolds argues from word formation and prosody for lexical compounding below the magnitude boundary.

curious.title: Numbers like twenty-one and ninety-nine
curious.summary: Numbers such as twenty-one, forty-two and ninety-nine join a tens word and a ones word.
curious.body:
Twenty-one is twenty plus one. Forty-two is forty plus two, and ninety-nine is ninety plus nine. Each is typically written with a hyphen and counts as one word.

A number like forty-three also supplies the base for forty-third. A version with and inside, like forty and three, would be a different structure, not the ordinary word.
curious.try: Turn forty-three into forty-third. Which part of the word changes?

teacher.summary: Explains two-part numbers from 21 to 99 as single lexical units formed from a decade and a single digit.
teacher.explain: A compound basic numerative is a decade word followed by a single-digit word, typically hyphenated: twenty-one is 20 + 1. It's a lexical compound below the magnitude boundary, with the same distribution as simple basic numeratives (determiner, factor, addition). Forty-three expresses one lexicalized sum and supplies a base for forty-third. It requires a decade base with a single-digit addition. A coordinator inside, as in forty and three, produces a separate structure and isn't the ordinary lexical compound. This dictionary marks this account as provisional.
teacher.terms: Numerative is this dictionary's term for number words, where a textbook may say numeral.

contrasts.note: Internal coordination isn't part of the ordinary compound.
The pattern requires a single-digit addition to a decade.

watch_for: A learner might put and inside a number from 21 to 99, as in twenty and one.
A learner might try to build a number such as twenty-ten, when the pattern requires a single-digit addition to a decade.
teacher.activity: Give students decade cards and single-digit cards. They build every number they can from 21 to 99, hyphenate each one, and say its ordinal.

child.hook: How do we say numbers like twenty-one?
child.explain: Some numbers are made of two parts. Twenty-one is twenty and one put together. We typically write a hyphen between the parts.
child.play: Pick a tens word, like forty. Add each ones word to it, from one to nine. Say each number and write it with a hyphen.

checked.note: Fixed: curious.summary no longer claims every number from twenty-one to ninety-nine is tens plus ones (exact tens like thirty fall outside the pattern); hyphenation stated as typical, as in the entry; removed the 'common name' claim for compound numeral from teacher.terms; sharpened the twenty-ten watch_for to the entry's constraint. Second round: fixed curious.body, which said forty-three takes an ordinal ending because it is a single word; it now says, as this dictionary does, that forty-three supplies the base for forty-third. Also fixed (unflagged): the child example The page is ninety-nine used the number as a label, not a cardinality, and now counts years.

cite: Reynolds, Brett, ed. 2026. "Compound Basic Numerative (Decade + Single-digit)." English Constructionary. https://brettreynolds.ca/constructionary/linguist/numerative-compound-basic-001/ (snapshot 2026-11-19, 5c11b28).
